summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplantation for cryptogenic cirrhosis, immunosuppressed on sirolimus, was admitted with fevers, malaise, and confusion over two days, along with a two-week productive cough. He had no focal chest findings but exhibited leukocytosis and crackles on exam. Chest imaging showed interstitial markings suggestive of atypical pneumonia or congestion. Despite negative cultures and viral panels, he was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics for presumed community-acquired pneumonia given his high infection risk. He also developed acute kidney injury with creatinine rising to 2.1, attributed to cardiorenal syndrome, supported by elevated pro-BNP and radiographic congestion, though echocardiography was limited. Diuresis with Lasix improved renal function, and the diuretic was discontinued prior to discharge due to concern for over-diuresis. His mental status improved, and he was discharged home after five days on continued home medications with follow-up planned for renal and cardiac evaluation.
